notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on: (1) the original lens (NRHP: lens-lantern with no Fresnel; USLHS: fourth-order Fresnel); (2) start of work (NRHP: after July 1903 plans; LighthouseFriends: November 1903, with temporary light 1 Dec 1903); (3) the size of the 1924 building (NRHP 34 by 20 ft; LighthouseFriends 20 by 36 ft); (4) the age of the lantern (NRHP: original 1904; 1922 Bulletin: orders for new 4th-order lanterns); (5) first keeper's name (NRHP John O. Carlson; USLHS John A. Carlson); NRHP spells the engineer Langfelt once and Langfist once. USLHS roster starts 1905 though the light was lit in 1904. Roster rows come from USLHS (NARA registers via Kraig Anderson); the Lighthouse Board and Bulletin volumes available offline do not cover 1902-1914 reports, so the 1904 Board report was not read. The Prohibition-era boat anecdote and the family quarrels are from a 1990 Alaska Magazine article as quoted in the NRHP nomination, undated and unnamed; the NRHP says the keepers 'rowed out', LighthouseFriends says 'two keepers' found the boat. LighthouseFriends also says an assistant keeper's wife was murdered in a family conflict: deliberately left out as unsourced there and not corroborated. Efficiency flag: Bulletin 1915 list matched by position (District 16, Guard Island, John C. Johnson) plus the 1912-1917 index entry; the index gives 195 as page. Bulletin 1924 'fog signals improved' item is from an issue before 1 May 1924 (column-interleaved OCR; read by position). Commissioner 1921 and 1918 page numbers: 1918 p. 71 confirmed by scan data, 1921 scan page 678 only (printed page unconfirmed). No newspaper search succeeded (Chronicling America search timed out). Fog-signal start 'Type C diaphone' in 1924 per NRHP. Characteristic and range not confirmed from a source read, so left out of facts.light.
